chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Ays, from Najm ibn Huteym, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever intends fasting, then visits his brother and asks him to break his fast in his presence, let him break it, and let him bring him joy, for it is recorded for him on that day as ten days' [reward].
This is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for inviting a fasting person to break their fast?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the social etiquette of hosting a fasting brother by linking the act of providing iftar to the spiritual reward of ten days of fasting, as derived from the Quranic principle of tenfold recompense. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining physical sustenance with emotional care ('bringing joy') to maximize spiritual merit. The hadith serves as a practical guide for strengthening kinship ties through charitable hospitality during Ramadan.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Barqy, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Ays, from Najam Bin Huteym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who intends the Fasting, then goes over to his brother, so he asks him that he should break in his presence, so let him break, and let him enter the joy upon him, for it (the Fast) of that day would be Counted for him as ten days;
and these are the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [6:160] Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten like it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqiy from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-‘Is from Najm ibn Hutaym who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If one decides to fast, and then goes to visit his brother (in belief) who offers to serve him food, he should break his fast for the happiness of his host and due to his request. This will be counted equal to ten days of fasting
as Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has said, ‘One who does one good deed will receive tenfold reward for the same.’ [6:161] ”
